correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the graph definition and face/facet condition for each n∈{6,7,8,9}. Independently implemented an exhaustive C++17 enumeration of all independent four-sets, exact complements/subfaces, descending-dimension greedy vertex-toggle pairings, complete reoriented Hasse DAG and Kahn acyclicity test. All counts equal the original package: (indep4,nonempty faces,incidences,matching pairs,critical) = (48,2545,12876,1257,{0:1,4:30}); (154,13463,87038,6699,{0:1,6:64}); (384,60578,467728,30242,{0:1,8:93}); (810,254369,2255346,127119,{0:1,10:130}). The topological sorting visited every nonempty face. Forman acyclic matching yields CW models with one 0-cell and exclusively d≥4 cells, whose attaching maps land in a point, hence the asserted integral wedge equivalences; mod-2 ranks alone would not justify them. Complements of distinct independent 4-sets are equal-sized facets of dimension 2n−5; nonzero homology in 2n−8 implies failure of pure shellability. Checked n=5 excluded K5,5 coincidence. The certificate is exhaustive only for these four widths; no infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The graphs are a natural highly symmetric cubic family. Agarwal–Basak (2026) Problem 26 specifically motivates cut/total-cut topology for Möbius ladders. The n=5 total-four-cut instance is already a complete-bipartite coincidence, while n=6..9 are the first four nontrivial consecutive widths, spanning both bipartite and nonbipartite graphs. Exact integral sphere-wedge decompositions (not just Betti numbers), a full acyclic matching and non-shellability constitute a useful natural finite classification/benchmark at the next cut parameter, even without an all-n theorem or paper-sized advance. Correctness, novelty and reproducibility alone are not used as the motivation.
residual_risks: The statement treats a finite interval and does not establish general 4-cut topology for arbitrary Möbius ladders.
These finite numerical invariants have value as a naturally motivated cutoff but are not claimed to imply a uniform recurrence or equivariant homotopy result.
